risks.note: Management flags that a sudden correction in air or sea freight rates can compress revenue and margin on spot cargo. Mitigants cited are long-term customer relationships, carrier partnerships, value-added services and pricing discipline - but as a forwarder the Company's revenue is directly geared to freight pricing cycles.

Trade restrictions, tariff measures, Red Sea disruptions and geopolitical events may affect cargo flows and freight demand. The threat section adds that tariff measures by major economies can cause route disruptions, higher logistics costs, shipment delays and demand uncertainty in export sectors. Mitigants: diversified trade lanes, multimodal capability and network flexibility.

Lower global or domestic trade activity may reduce shipment volumes; a synchronised global slowdown could both cut volumes and push freight rates down. Mitigants are a diversified customer base and sectoral diversification. FY26 already saw revenue fall on softer global freight demand.

risks.risk: Structurally thin margins and the margin-expansion imperative
risks.note: Management itself flags net profit margins at 0.07% as reflecting the cost-competitive nature of freight forwarding. Expanding margins depends on executing a disciplined shift toward higher-value services (warehousing, break bulk, project cargo) and on operating leverage over the existing branch infrastructure - so earnings are highly sensitive to any slip in mix or volume.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity from MNC and technology-enabled forwarders
risks.note: Increased competition from multinational and technology-enabled logistics players; the threats section names tech-enabled digital freight platforms, large MNC forwarders (DHL, Kuehne+Nagel, CEVA) and domestic full-service operators in an already fragmented market. Defence rests on service differentiation, customer relationships and integrated solutions.

risks.risk: Counterparty and credit risk on receivables
risks.note: Delayed collections or defaults may impact cash flows in a business that funds customer freight ahead of collection. Mitigants are credit assessment procedures and receivables monitoring; the Company made receivables reduction and overdue-balance control an explicit FY26 focus area.

System outages, cyber threats or data breaches may disrupt operations - a material exposure given the Company has migrated its freight, warehousing, customs, billing and financial processes onto a single cloud-based ERP. Mitigants cited are the cloud-based ERP itself, cybersecurity protocols and backup systems.

risks.risk: Regulatory, compliance and talent execution risk
risks.note: Changes in customs, GST, IATA and other regulatory requirements may increase compliance obligations, and navigating evolving customs rules, GST amendments, IATA changes and trade-treaty modifications requires constant vigilance. Compounding this, attrition of experienced logistics professionals may affect execution capability, and rapid demand spikes can stress operational bandwidth, staffing and IT infrastructure.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural tailwinds in Indian logistics - policy support, infrastructure development, increasing formalisation, and growth in manufacturing and EXIM trade
- Government initiatives such as the National Logistics Policy and PM GatiShakti improving logistics efficiency and India's competitiveness as a manufacturing and export hub
- 'China+1' supply-chain realignment accelerating India's emergence as a key manufacturing and sourcing hub, expected to drive sustained demand for freight forwarding and cross-border logistics
- Growing customer preference for asset-light, network-driven logistics players that can scale efficiently and deliver integrated end-to-end solutions
- Rising outsourcing of supply chain functions, higher trade volumes and growing demand for integrated logistics services
- India's e-commerce market targeting USD 200 billion by 2026, generating an exponential increase in high-frequency international freight forwarding demand
- Growing trade flows with Africa, Southeast Asia and ASEAN markets opening new corridors and customer segments
- India's National Infrastructure Pipeline, defence modernisation and industrial capex driving project cargo demand that rewards specialised forwarders
- Increasing formalisation of supply chains and demand for integrated logistics creating opportunity in warehousing and contract logistics, where Flomic has ~13.8 lakh sq. ft.
- Margin lever: mix shift into higher-value services (warehousing, break bulk, project cargo) plus operating leverage on the existing branch infrastructure, against net profit margins of 0.07%
- Direct sales model adding approximately 60 new customers every month, which management says yields better revenue quality and higher net margins than sub-agent models
- Headwind: competitive intensity from tech-enabled digital freight startups, MNC forwarders (DHL, Kuehne+Nagel, CEVA) and domestic full-service operators
- Headwind: tariff measures by major economies, Red Sea disruptions and geopolitical volatility affecting cargo flows, particularly in export sectors such as textiles, footwear, engineering goods and marine products
- Headwind: a synchronised global slowdown could reduce trade volumes and put downward pressure on freight rates

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Flomic is an asset-light logistics services business and this bundle discloses no manufacturing capex, no named project with a commissioning timeline and no rupee capex quantum. Expansion is expressed as network footprint: during FY2025-26 the Company's pan-India presence was expanded to 18 branches across key gateway ports and commercial hubs, supported by 30+ warehousing facilities with a warehousing footprint of approximately 13.8 lakh sq. ft. across major logistics corridors, and a multi-port presence covering Mumbai (JNPT), Chennai, Mundra, Kolkata, Nhava Sheva and other key ports. The other stated investment is in the proprietary cloud-based ERP platform, which the Chairman describes as continued investment in a unified freight forwarding, transportation, warehousing, customs, billing and financial processes platform that enables scalable growth without a proportional increase in operating costs. Forward-looking expansion intent in this bundle is directional rather than project-specific: expanding presence across key logistics hubs, scaling warehousing, project logistics and break-bulk capabilities, and strengthening CFS and air cargo operations. The Chairman explicitly frames the asset-light model as one that scales with minimal capital intensity.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over four decades of experience in international freight forwarding and supply chain management (45th Annual Report), giving long-standing relationships with global shipping lines and carrier allocation leverage
- Asset-light and scalable business model that allows the Company to scale operations with minimal capital intensity
- Diversified base of 5,000+ active customers with strong repeat business, which the Company cites as reducing concentration risk
- Revenue diversified across export, import and warehousing streams rather than a single mode
- Proprietary cloud-based ERP platform integrating freight forwarding, warehousing, transportation, customs, CRM, billing and financial accounting on one operating platform, enabling growth without proportional cost increases
- Membership of international logistics networks WCA, JCTrans and Prolog, providing a global partner ecosystem and allocation leverage
- Pan-India network of 18 branches plus 30+ warehouses (~13.8 lakh sq. ft.) at gateway ports and commercial hubs, giving a wide export-cargo catchment
- Integrated 'one-stop' capability spanning air, land and sea, including hard-to-execute niches such as project cargo, break bulk and exhibition/event logistics
- Demonstrated complex-project execution capability, evidenced by a project cargo movement from India to Nigeria of over 850 metric tonnes across 115 packages

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: High reliance on single bank (ICICI); limited financial transparency; small scale exposes to client concentration risk; no public financial statements to verify profitability

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The Rs.45 Cr loan facility is entirely from ICICI Bank — indicating extreme banking concentration, which is a hidden liquidity risk if credit lines are tightened

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Progressively shift the revenue mix toward higher-margin segments - warehousing, break bulk and project cargo - while sustaining growth in the core freight forwarding business
- Stay asset-light and integrated: scale operations with minimal capital intensity while maintaining financial discipline and flexibility
- Expand presence across key logistics hubs and in high-growth logistics segments
- Scale warehousing, project logistics and break-bulk capabilities
- Strengthen CFS and air cargo operations
- Increase wallet share with existing customers through integrated, one-stop service offerings
- Enhance …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body: - [Industry] India's logistics cost has fallen to 7.97% of GDP; the deck frames policy reform and digital integration as tailwinds that will lift outsourcing and freight volumes and favour integrated players like Flomic.
